question: The accuracy of measurement by a try square is about:
solution:
The correct answer is __0.002 mm per 10 mm length__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The try square__ is a precision tool used for checking the squareness of objects.
 
• It is commonly used in woodworking and metalworking to measure right angles.
 
• The accuracy of measurement of a try square is approximately __0.002 mm per 10 mm length__.
 
• Try squares are made of steel or other durable materials to ensure reliability.
 
• Regular calibration is essential to maintain the accuracy of a try square.
 
• They are available in different sizes to cater to various measurement needs.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Micrometer:**

 
 
• A micrometer is a measuring instrument used for precise measurements of small dimensions.
 
• Its accuracy is usually in the range of 0.01 mm or finer.
 
 
 
• **Vernier Caliper:**
 
 
• A Vernier caliper is a versatile instrument for measuring internal and external dimensions as well as depths.
 
• Its accuracy is typically 0.02 mm.
 
 
 
• **Dial Gauge:**
 
 
• A dial gauge is used to measure small linear distances with high accuracy.
 
• It is commonly used in engineering applications for alignment and measurement.
